sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- web_search: Use for web research questions. Prefer {queries:[...]} with 2-4 varied angles over a single query for broader coverage. Omit provider unless explicitly overriding the configured default.
- source_check: Gather structured source evidence and passage-level citations for manual semantic review of a claim.
- fetch_content: Use to fetch URL content, direct images, GitHub repos, and videos.
- get_search_content: Use after web_search, source_check, or fetch_content to retrieve stored content via responseId. Use findText to locate passages without paging through the full content.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/app/local/yh/AGENTS.md">
You are working for vLLM issue. Here are some important things to be remembered. 

- vllm is installed with editable install at /app/local/yh/vllm
- any python installation just do `python3 -m pip` (we are in a confined container)


1. To reinstall vllm
python3 -m pip uninstall -y vllm
rm -rf build/ && rm -rf .deps && rm -rf vllm.egg-info && rm -rf vllm/*.so
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950 python3 setup.py develop

2. An example to run lm-eval (gsm8k)
- if lm_eval is not installed, install with `python3 -m pip install lm_eval[api]`

lm_eval   --model local-chat-completions   --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8020/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000   --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}'   --batch_size auto   --tasks gsm8k   --num_fewshot 25   --apply_chat_template

3. Interact with github using gh (if gh is not setup, prompt the user to do it)

4. For vllm bench serve configuration, refer to the official docs: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/cli/bench/serve/

5. Use internet search to help research about topics/relevant information and grounding facts. Do not simply guess and assume. 

6. When working on an issue, use a new workdir to properly document and house all testing artifacts
- properly document all your findings in a way it's easy to read and retrieve
- all artifacts, testing scritps to be put into the issue workdir

7. When GPU is occupy, and it's not own by you. Stop and report to user. Otherwise, you can make the decision to stop it. 

8. Utilize subagents for long running tasks/side jobs like implementation so you can focus on coordinating and ensure correctness.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.description: Search the web with OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, Parallel MCP, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, DuckDuckGo, Perplexity, Gemini, Kimi, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, Bocha, XCrawl, Baizhi. Provider arrays run simultaneously; all searches eligible allowed providers (OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, Perplexity, Gemini, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Bocha); explicit-only allowed providers (Parallel MCP, DuckDuckGo, Kimi, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, XCrawl, Baizhi) remain excluded. The default workflow is none: it returns bounded source-linked search results or provider answers without a curator or generated summary, identifies the providers used, and stores full results for retrieval by responseId. For comprehensive research, prefer queries (plural) with 2-4 varied angles over a single query. When includeContent is true, full page content is fetched in the background. Set workflow to "summary-review" to open the curator with an auto-generated summary draft or "auto-summary" to generate a summary without the browser curator. The configured provider is used when provider is omitted or set to auto; omit provider unless explicitly overriding it.

queries.description: Multiple queries searched concurrently (up to three at a time), each returning source-linked search results or a provider answer. Prefer this for research — vary phrasing, scope, and angle across 2-4 queries to maximize coverage. Good: ['React vs Vue performance benchmarks 2026', 'React vs Vue developer experience comparison', 'React ecosystem size vs Vue ecosystem']. Bad: ['React vs Vue', 'React vs Vue comparison', 'React vs Vue review'] (too similar, redundant results).

toolsAdded.name: source_check
toolsAdded.description: Gather web sources for a claim and return a bounded machine-readable research artifact with exact passage citations for manual review.

fetchContent.description: Fetch up to 5 result pages for exact passage extraction.

domainFilter.description: Limit to domains; prefix with - to exclude.

provider.description: Search provider or non-empty list of allowed providers to search simultaneously; all searches eligible allowed providers (OpenAI, Brave, Parallel, TinyFish, Search1API, Searchinfinity, Querit, Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, SearXNG, Perplexity, Gemini, Exa, SERPdive, Kagi, Ollama, Bocha); explicit-only allowed providers (Parallel MCP, DuckDuckGo, Kimi, Anysearch, xAI, Mistral, Bright Data, SerpBase, SerpApi, Serper, Serply, Valyu, XCrawl, Baizhi) remain excluded

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description: Fetch URL(s). Available modes: readable (default): extract readable content as markdown; raw: return the exact textual body using direct HTTP only; answer: answer a prompt using only fetched content. Direct image URLs return resized image content when supported by the selected mode. Supports YouTube transcripts, GitHub repositories, PDFs, and local videos when supported by the selected mode. Full original content is stored for retrieval with get_search_content.

forceClone.description: Force cloning large GitHub repositories that exceed the size threshold

prompt.description: Question or instruction for video analysis, or the page-local question required by answer mode.

mode.description: Fetch mode. readable (default): extract readable content as markdown; raw: return the exact textual body using direct HTTP only; answer: answer a prompt using only fetched content.

answerModel.description: Optional provider/model-id override for answer mode. Defaults to fetch.answerProvider + fetch.answerModel when configured, otherwise the current Pi model.

timestamp.description: Extract video frame(s) at a timestamp or time range. Single: '1:23:45', '23:45', or '85' (seconds). Range: '23:41-25:00' extracts evenly-spaced frames across that span (default 6). Use frames with ranges to control density; single+frames uses a fixed 5s interval. YouTube requires yt-dlp + ffmpeg; local videos require ffmpeg. Use a range when you know the approximate area but not the exact moment — you'll get a contact sheet to visually identify the right frame.

frames.description: Number of frames to extract. Use with timestamp range for custom density, with single timestamp to get N frames at 5s intervals, or alone to sample across the entire video. Requires yt-dlp + ffmpeg for YouTube, ffmpeg for local video.

model.description: Override the Gemini model for video/YouTube analysis (e.g. 'gemini-3.6-flash'). Defaults to config or gemini-3.6-flash.

auth.description: Opt into an authFetch profile for local browser-cookie fetching. Use a profile name, or true only when exactly one profile exists.

proxy.description: http(s) or socks proxy URL (e.g. http://host:port or socks5h://host:port) used for this fetch. Needed when the target is unreachable directly; localhost and NO_PROXY hosts always bypass the proxy. Empty string forces direct access.

toolsAdded.name: get_search_content
toolsAdded.description: Retrieve bounded pages of full stored search results or fetched content, or find matching passages, from a previous web_search, source_check, or fetch_content call.

responseId.description: The responseId from web_search, source_check, or fetch_content

queryIndex.description: Get content for query at index

urlIndex.description: Get content for URL at index

offset.description: Character offset in stored search or fetched URL content (default 0). Ignored when findText is supplied.

limit.description: Requested maximum stored-content characters (default and max use maxInlineContentChars). Search-page continuation guidance shares the global output cap and may reduce returnedChars. Ignored when findText is supplied.

findText.description: Text or texts to find in the selected stored content. When supplied, offset and limit are ignored.

findMode.description: Matching mode for findText (default: case-insensitive). Requires findText.

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

toolsAdded.name: subagents_enable
toolsAdded.description: Enable pi-subagents delegation and management tools without launching work. Call when delegation is authorized by the current request or applicable user/project instructions, or when managing existing runs. Direct execution is the default; complexity alone never authorizes delegation. Full tools are available on the next model request.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Native pi-subagents supervisor channel. Use reply/pending/status to answer child subagent requests without overriding pi-intercom.

# mimo-explore — MiMo exploration / experiment / research index

One-time reorg 2026-09-26: the seven MiMo workdirs below moved here from `/app/local/yh/` as
siblings (dir names unchanged). Absolute refs in `.md/.sh/.py/.txt` were repointed to
`/app/local/yh/mimo-explore/<name>`; sibling-relative `../<name>` refs still resolve (same parent).
Issue workdirs and the live A/B stay top-level (operator decision) and were not touched.

## Front matter

| folder | kind | status | one-line verdict | key doc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lmcache-mimo-v26` | experiment | COMPLETE | Cross-replica LMCache KV transfer proven — final probe campaign 19/19, HMA×MTP 2×2 letters all gates 7/7 | [RESULTS.md](lmcache-mimo-v26/RESULTS.md) |
| `aiter-unified-ab` | experiment | CLOSED | Unified-attn beats DiffKV: TPOT −16%/−18% (p50/p95), TTFT p50 −29%, accuracy/KV parity | [REPORT.md](aiter-unified-ab/REPORT.md) |
| `kvfp8-ab` | experiment | COMPLETE | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` silently buys no capacity (−0.01% vs expected ×2); store stays bf16 | [report.md](kvfp8-ab/report.md) |

| `dflash-ab` | experiment | BLOCKED-record | Official DFlash drafter blocked on DFlash×LMCache KV-layout guard (0/3 boots); MTP control reproduced Cell A | [final_dflash_run.md](dflash-ab/final_dflash_run.md) |

Out of scope: `../issue-52109` and `../issue-57030` are NON-MiMo issue workdirs (stay top-level).

## Experiments

### lmcache-mimo-v26 — LMCache cross-replica KV + HMA×MTP ablation
- Probe campaign closed **19/19 asserts**; cross-replica hit proven 4/4 runs: pxfer **66.0 ms (×4.66
  vs control)**, ext_hits 5888/5922, replica-2 local store untouched (local_hits=0).
- HMA×MTP 2×2 letters a/b/c/d all gates **7/7**; letter a (MTP×3) gsm8k .9765 bit-identical across
  store/retrieve/xreplica passes; letter d (MTP×3 + HMA on) clean 7/7.
- LMCache-served warm ≈ **×4 vs cold** at ~6k-token prefill. STATUS: COMPLETE 2026-09-23/24.

### aiter-unified-ab — ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN vs TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV
- UA wins: TPOT p50 **−16.1%** (4.280→3.592 ms), TTFT p50 **−29.4%** (194.3→137.1 ms), gsm8k −0.15pp
  inside ±1.0pp gate, MTP acceptance 0.669→0.666 parity; boot gates 10/10. Status CLOSED.
- Two infra fixes were prerequisites: mimo_v2 explicit-backend call contract + aiter PR #3698
  (unified-attention V-load OOB), and per-side head geometry in `reshape_and_cache_flash` (RC-W2).
- vllm_bench addendum (LMCache ON, 154k-in/1k-out): UA+`--block-size 16` TPOT **−84% (6.3×)**,
  TTFT −37%, output t/s 2.95× — block-size 16 mandatory (UA's preferred 64 breaks LMCache transfer).

### kvfp8-ab + kv-dtype-rootcause — can a non-fp8 vLLM reuse an fp8 KV store?
- A/B/C cells: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` bought nothing — budget 872,393 vs 872,520 tok (**−0.01%**,
  expected ≈×2); `lmcache describe` bf16 125,440 B/token in all cells → true fp8 store never materialized.
- Cell C cleanly reused B's store (**14,592 external hits**) only because the data was bf16-layout;
  the strict cross-dtype read stayed untested.
- Root cause (two-stage): `mimo_v2.py` construction sites never pass `cache_config` → silent no-op;
  DiffKV has no fp8 path either. Fix = upstream **PR #58128** (open; RFC #58638).

### dflash-ab — official DFlash drafter vs embedded MTP (real-data A/B)
- Arm E (MTP×3 control): full pass, reproduced historical Cell A within noise — 80/80, acceptance
  1.8298 vs 1.8545, mean TTFT −3.18%, output t/s −1.46% (noise floor documented).
- Arm D (DFlash ×7): **BLOCKED, 0/3 boots** — dies deterministically at the DFlash×LMCache
  `REGISTER_KV_CACHE` dim-0-padding guard (`NL_X_NB_BS_NH_CS` unsupported); D-vs-E answer does not
  exist under the mandated LMCache-on recipe.
- Drafter KV cost (pre-death boot lines): default mode D 830,585 vs E 872,520 tokens = **−4.80%**.

## Research

### mimo-v26-opt-research — serving-optimization synthesis
- `OPPORTUNITIES.md` (2026-09-25, research-only): master ranking **P1–P14** for this 2×gfx950 +
  LMCache + HMA + MTP stack, plus C1–C6 self-corrections (DiffKV + SWA-hybrid attention, not full
  attention; MTP = one layer iterated ×3).
- `COUNSEL_2026-09-26_nextstep_after_ua.md`: 3-lens (researcher/oracle/reviewer) next-step opinions
  + contributor-verified external status table (#58128 OPEN and gaining, #35461 MERGED).
- `nextstep_1_upstream.md` → `nextstep_2_local.md` → `nextstep_3_verdict.md`: headline = promote P2,
  a zero-run root-cause read of the ext-hit → local-APC backfill gap under HMA, before any GPU letter.

- Ordered `patches/` + byte-gated `files/`: base `29468dde8b` = PR #58262 (MXFP4 gfx942) + PR #58142
  (paired loader) + local UA delta (`cache_kernels.cu` v-head geometry, mimo_v2 MTP select), plus
  aiter `30/40-*.patch` for `amd_aiter 0.1.22.post1` (`patch -p1` from site-packages).
  Verification: `ua-recreate/RESULT.md` **GATE=ALL_PASS** (apply rc=0, `cmp` == staged snapshot);
  owner-build runtime sanity gsm8k strict 0.9727 / flex 0.9719 PASS vs reference band.
- pip-install addendum: `cache_kernels.cu` compiles only into `_C_stable_libtorch` → single-`.so`
  rebuild; dist-packages `.py` drops guarded by pristine-sha preflights @29468 (fail-closed).
- Repo state (`RESULT.md` §BRANCH DISPATCH): branch **`custom/ua-mimo-gfx942`** @ 3430f806f0 pushed to
  EmbeddedLLM/vllm (remote sha == local); main @ 0f2a15c9 untouched (+2 modified files); stash exists
  as `stash@{0}` "ua-delta on main@0f2a15c9" + byte-backup patch — return via `git switch main && git stash pop`.

## Notes

- `../aiter-online-tune-ab` = **AITER_ONLINE_TUNE A/B**, ACTIVE-elsewhere (live chain owns that dir;

# OPPORTUNITIES — MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL serving optimization (research synthesis)

**Status:** research-only deliverable, 2026-09-25. No experiments run under this task.
**Sources:** `research/R1_model_ecosystem.md`, `R2_rocm_serving_knobs.md`, `R3_spec_decode_mtp.md`,
`R4_kv_cache_topology.md` (full cards, evidence, citations live there). Parent did NOT re-verify
web claims; parent DID re-verify all local `[F]` claims below (§0).
**Tags:** [F]=fetched/local-read verified · [S]=search-snippet only (re-verify before acting) · [I]=inference.

---

## 0. Parent cross-checks & corrections to our own prior record (2026-09-25, local greps)

| # | Claim under test | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | We serve FP8 weights natively (FINDINGS "BF16" was misleading) | **CONFIRMED** | startup: `quantization=fp8, dtype=torch.bfloat16` (= activations) + `+quant_fp8` custom-ops; official config = `store_dtype: mxfp4, weight_block_size [128,128]` (R1) — no "FP8 checkpoint to adopt", *verify-only* |
| C2 | Attention is DiffKV + SWA-hybrid, **NOT full attention** | **CONFIRMED** | log `Using TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV` (mimo_v2.py:322); `hybrid_layer_pattern`/`sliding_window_size` applied per-layer (mimo_v2.py:298,464); official config = 39×SWA(window 128, sinks) + 9 global (R1/R2). Our run.sh note "`attention_chunk_size is None`" stays true **for that one vLLM field** (it gates HMA auto-disable branch) but the **"full attention" gloss was wrong** — the model is hybrid underneath; our 6 KV groups = 9-layer global group + SWA groups |
| C3 | Scheduler budget = untouched default | **CONFIRMED** | `Chunked prefill is enabled with max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (scheduler.py:302) |
| C4 | MTP draft = ONE trained layer iterated 3× | **CONFIRMED** | `num_mtp_layers = 1` hardcode, mimo_v2_mtp.py:173 (layers 1–2 of `num_nextn_predict_layers=3` unloaded) |
| C5 | KV cache dtype = auto (BF16) ⇒ fp8-KV card is a real delta | **CONFIRMED** | startup `kv_cache_dtype=auto` |
| C6 | R3's "extract our own per-position acceptance" gap | **ALREADY ANSWERED** | letters-D logs: `Per-position acceptance rate: 0.904, 0.643, 0.355` (and later window `0.962, 0.403, 0.098`). pos1 ≈ DeepSeek's 85–90% regime; **tails decay = exactly the layer0×K-reuse signature the cascade (P5b) targets** ⇒ P5b's cheap-verify criterion MET, no new run needed |

**Refinement to FINDINGS §ros1:** the 250k acceptance collapse was **mostly** workload artifact
(random tokens + temp 1.0; official sampling IS temp=1.0/top_p=0.95 — R1c4), but literature
(vLLM #47602: pos1 0.935→0.721 from 2k→30k) shows acceptance **genuinely decays with context** —
expect a real curve, re-measure on natural text (P8).

## 3. Cross-seam contradictions resolved (parent adjudication)

- **"full attention" vs SWA-hybrid (R1/R2 vs run.sh note):** resolved in §0-C2 — model is SWA-hybrid; only the *vLLM field* `attention_chunk_size` (HMA auto-disable gate) is None. Consequences: (i) our HMA ×2.25 > theoretical ×2 likely owes to SWA window- freeing (R4c6 hypothesis (i), now the leading one); (ii) group layout "exactly two groups … other cases not implemented" (hybrid-KV design doc) vs our SIX groups strengthens P2's coordinator suspect; (iii) P4's skip-layers flag explicitly targets sliding_window — arch is ideal (9 global + 39 window-128).
- **"BF16" (stack brief) vs fp8 checkpoint (R1) vs `dtype=bfloat16` (log):** activations bf16, weights fp8-block on mxfp4 store — all three true at different layers (§0-C1).
- **Acceptance-at-250k:** artifact (ros1) + genuine-but-modest ctx decay (#47602) — both, per §0 refinement; P8 measures the real curve.
- **Two speculative artifacts** (README conflates): embedded MTP (3 trained layers, we use 1) vs separate DFlash drafter (5 layers/7 tokens, official recipe) — distinct cards, P5a vs P5b.

## 7. Status updates (2026-09-25 post-synthesis — details: kv-dtype-rootcause/FINAL_rootcause.md, dflash-ab/report.md)
- **P4 → BLOCKED-ON-UPSTREAM; no-op proven (charge closed).** Budget ×1.0001 (872,393 vs 872,520 tok), store bf16 125,440 B/tok identical. Two-stage root cause locally proven: (i) `cache_config` never passed at `mimo_v2.py:377/397` + `mimo_v2_mtp.py:88` ctors (param defaults None → Attention gets None; engine INFO at `config/cache.py:362` honest only at CONFIG level); (ii) Triton-DiffKV has no fp8 kernel (`supported_kv_cache_dtypes=[auto,bfloat16]` + NotImplementedError guard :113 — PR #41797, sinks-era minimal fallback; model's direct enum pick bypasses `validate_configuration`). Fix upstream = open **PR #58128** (pool 1,365,757→2,731,530 = ×2.0003, GSM8K 0.933→0.943, needles pass; **TTFT +4–7% @16–32K, +15% @128K, decode flat**; GB10-tested, ROCm untested). tonyd2wild 3.3× → true dtype effect 1.8–2× (8,151 vs 14,780 B/tok) + their archived stock log = our symptom. Official AMD recipe (re-verified present) ships the flag ⇒ **no-op on stock builds** (record-high-value community note).
- **P5a → BLOCKED first-party (DFlash×LMCache):** 0/3 boots — drafter bucket ⇒ vLLM emits dim-0-padded probe rows (`Add 1 padding layers` warnings D-only; stride0 40960 vs 32768, layer 48, NL_X_NB_BS_NH_CS) and LMCache v0.5.3 rejects at REGISTER (`gpu_connector/utils.py:566`) → 300s timeout → engine dead. Live reproduction of today's **RFC #58638 / issue #58175** (hybrid-group padding; also −4.8% drafter KV budget pre-death). MTP×3 control (Arm E) passed, ≡ A within noise (acc 1.8298 vs 1.8545, prompt-set hash-identical). **RESOLVED 2026-09-25 (operator): DROPPED and its LMCache workaround not authorized — "if LMCache
doesn't work, ignore it; LMCache is a must."** DFlash stays shelved pending upstream #58207 / connector-format
support; artifacts + validated drafter (snapshot 5711b2) retained for a future re-evaluation. Perf-thread follow-ups
recorded from gh instead: **#58177** (BLOCK_M=32 prefill KV-load reuse: kernel 1.62–1.83×, TTFT −7…−12% @16–32K,
bitwise-identical; gate = is_cuda() + SM12x ⇒ NOT active on gfx950 as written) and **#58650** (ROCm-native
window-aware split-KV + occupancy launch for Triton DiffKV = the ROCm perf PR to watch/apply).
- P13 superseded (closed trace). R1c1 accuracy correction pending DFlash passing run (dflash dir now valid at snapshot 5711b2, 2.9G, config trailing-comma CONFIRMED at 3b38 = R1 Contradiction #2 resolved).
- Process: **gh CLI = GitHub interface from now on** (auth `vllmellm`; surfaced #58128/#58638 web missed). Scout 25-min timeout w/ zero output (3rd report-first lesson) → parent executed the trace inline; RC13 (output-binding clobber) hit once more but reports were pre-separable.

# issue-mimo-v25-fp8-qkv

MiMo-V2.5 fails to load on vLLM main (crash `1856 vs 1792` at any TP < 8).
Investigated, root-caused, fixed locally on a branch, and verified end-to-end at TP=4 (2026-09-17).

## Root cause in one line

The checkpoint's fused `qkv_proj` is **pre-sharded at `ckpt_tp = config.num_key_value_heads` (4)**:
each chunk is `[Q_c|K_c|V_c]` with its own fp8 scale grid (GA chunk 3392 rows / 27 scales, SWA chunk
3712 rows / 29 scales → 108 and 116 scale rows). `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` (from #45200) assumes **one
chunk per KV head**, which holds for Pro (8/8) and for V2.5's GA layers (4/4) but not for the SWA
layers (8 KV heads, 4 chunks) → `116 // 8 = 14` scale rows → 1792 rows for an 1856-row slice →
`RuntimeError: 1856 vs 1792`. TP=8 additionally needs kv replication (#46755).

## Fix status

- Branch **`mimo-v25-fp8-qkv-scale-grid`** in `/app/local/yh/vllm`, two commits on top of
  `9854b580df` (= current main): **`7fd1321b38`** (checkpoint-chunk geometry, the actual fix),
  **`c1a45ad116`** (KV-head replication, so TP=8 works), **`01e46ad89a`** (MTP draft loader, so spec
  decode shards the same way), plus a review pass: **`13056bb405`** (`cdiv`, `ValueError` for layout
  mismatches) and **`6535b22150`** (in-tree unit test,
  `tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py`, 19 cases). Patch
  `vllm-mimo-v25-scale-grid.patch` covers all five.
- **Verified end-to-end at TP=4 on this box**: loads in ~10 min (was: crash at ~105 s) and answers
  correctly (`17*23` → `391`, `Canberra`, `150`, correct Python one-liner); gsm8k 25-shot
  exact_match **0.9704 flexible / 0.9712 strict ± 0.005 on the full 1319-sample test set**
  (`gsm8k_full/`; 0.985 on 200, 0.95 on 40).
- **TP=2 works** end-to-end as well (gsm8k(200) 0.99 ± 0.007). TP=1 is not runnable here only
  because 293 GiB of weights do not fit a 288 GiB device.
- **TP=8 + `--enable-expert-parallel` also works** (second commit): loads in ~3 min, answers
  correctly, gsm8k 0.985 ± 0.009 on 200 samples (`gsm8k_tp8ep_limit200/`); `--enable-expert-parallel` alone does *not* help — the limit is on the attention side,
  so KV-head replication is what unblocks it (same feature as upstream #46755).
- Verified offline: real tensors exact at TP=4 (relL2 0.0000) and at TP=8 for GA (0.0000), ≤ 0.011
  elsewhere; synthetic GA/SWA/Pro × TP 1/2/4/8 ≤ 0.028; the old reading (`ckpt_tp = num_kv_heads`)
  is detectably off (1.05).
- Corroborated by SGLang's loader for the same checkpoint (`load_mimo_v2_qkv_proj_weight`,
  `get_mimo_v2_fused_qkv_expected_tp_size == num_key_value_heads`).

# issue-mimo-v26-mxfp4-gfx942

**Q:** can gfx942 (MI300X) run MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL's MXFP4 MoE on the W4A16 kernel
(`AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16`), the way DeepSeek-V4-Flash does?

**A:** yes, with a **vLLM-only change**; no aiter change is required.

* MiMo's router is *ungrouped* sigmoid + `e_score_correction_bias`
  (`n_group=1`, `topk_method=noaux_tc`) → classified `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3 (2)`,
  which `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` rejects.
* aiter's **flat** top-k implements that router natively — `score_mode="sigmoid"`
  with a bias, returning the unbiased sigmoid scores, renormalized — since 0.1.20
  (ROCm/aiter#4688), and the pinned `v0.1.22.post1` has it. So the fix is: accept
  the family in the gate and ask for `sigmoid` (no other call-site surgery).
* Both checkpoints work this way: Flash (256 experts) and **Pro (384)**, which the
  *grouped* kernel could not serve because it caps at 256 experts.
* DeepSeek-V4 works for the analogous reason: `sqrtsoftplus` is implemented in the
  flat kernel and `DeepseekV4 (100)` is in the allow-list.

The grouped-route workaround (`num_expert_group = topk_group = 2`, all groups
kept, so selection degenerates to a global top-k over `sigmoid(logits) + bias` —
verified `MATCH` against a torch reference) remains valid but is only needed on
aiter < 0.1.20; it is not the PR.

## Routing kernel choice (flat, not grouped)

Both MiMo-V2.6 checkpoints use the same ungrouped sigmoid + correction-bias
router; sigmoid + bias exists in **two** aiter kernels, and which one we call
decides expert-count support:

| | flat `topk()` | `grouped_topk()` |
|---|---|---|
| expert cap | `n_cols < 32768` | `assert n_cols <= 256` |
| sigmoid + bias | ✓ since aiter 0.1.20 (ROCm/aiter#4688, 2026-08-14) | ✓ always |
| reached when | `use_grouped_topk=False`, i.e. `n_group == 1` (MiMo) | real grouping (`n_group > 1`) |

Checked in `aiter/ops/triton/moe/moe_routing/topk.py`: the 256 assert is still on
upstream `main`, flat `sigmoid` is contained in tags v0.1.20 / v0.1.21 / v0.1.22 /

- Root cause: fused `qkv_proj` checkpoint is pre-sharded at `ckpt_tp = num_key_value_heads` (4 chunks), but `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` assumed one chunk per KV head → wrong fp8 scale-grid slicing on SWA layers (8 KV heads, 4 chunks).

**`issue-mimo-v26-mxfp4-gfx942`** — can MI300X (gfx942) run **V2.6**'s MXFP4 MoE on the W4A16 kernel?
- Root cause: MiMo's router is *ungrouped* sigmoid + correction bias (`n_group=1`, `noaux_tc`) → vLLM gate rejects it for the monolithic kernel. Fix = vLLM-only (~20 lines): allow `RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3` + ask aiter's **flat** `topk()` for `score_mode="sigmoid"` (works since aiter 0.1.20; covers Flash 256 **and Pro 384** experts, which the grouped kernel's 252-cap can't). # ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN vs TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV — MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, gfx950
**Completed 2026-09-25, `CHAIN2_RC=0`.** Protocol: LMCache OFF, HMA ON, MTP×3, graphs ON, GPU0/TP1,
single delta = `--attention-backend`. All artifacts under this dir (`ab.sh t|u|stop|compare`).

## Verdict
`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` **wins on speed with accuracy intact**: TPOT **−16%/−18%** (p50/p95),
TTFT p50 **−29%**, gsm8k within noise (−0.15pp, gate ±1.0pp), MTP acceptance **0.669 → 0.666**
(parity), KV budget **8.72× → 8.71×** (parity), boot health 5/5 gates both arms.

## Headline table (U vs T; neg% = U better)
| metric | T = TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV | U = ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT p50 ms (n=8 cold) | 194.3 | 137.1 | **−29.4%** |
| TTFT p95 ms | 247.4 | 562.6 | +127.4% (1 single outlier, see §Caveats) |
| TPOT p50 ms | 4.280 | 3.592 | **−16.1%** |
| TPOT p95 ms | 5.006 | 4.092 | **−18.3%** |
| gsm8k exact_match flex (n=1319) | 0.9742 ±0.0044 | 0.9727 ±0.0045 | −0.0015 (**gate ≤0.01 ✓**) |
| gsm8k strict | 0.9750 | 0.9727 | −0.0023 ✓ |
| MTP acceptance (accepted/draft tok) | 0.669 | 0.666 | parity |
| KV budget (graphs) | 872,393 tok / 8.72× | 870,985 tok / 8.71× | −0.16% |
| boot tracebacks / faults | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | ✓ |
| warmup 400-tok TTFT (discarded) | 360.8 ms | 93.4 ms | −74% |
| bench TPOT raw range | 3.81–5.01 | 3.20–4.09 | U strictly lower on every paired request |

Gates (both arms): `backend_used=<expected>, hma=on (authoritative /server_info), mtp_log=seen,
boot_tracebacks=0, lmcache=absent` — **10/10 total**.

## How we got here (both arms required two infra patches)
Boot attempts 1–5 (see session log): (1) `set_head_size_v` class-hook assert — fixed by
contract-form edit in `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` (honor explicit `--attention-backend`;
call `set_head_size_v` only if defined — V width flows via KVCacheSpec `head_size_v`).
(2) **RC-K1** capture-time `Memory access fault` = aiter Triton `unified_attention` V-load/out-store
masked by K's head_size (192) → OOB writes ≥1536-token requests: fixed by upstream **aiter PR #3698**
applied locally (2 files, 3 hand-ported launcher hunks; `pr3698_*.rej/rej`+dual backups kept).
(3) **RC-W2** garbage text = native `reshape_and_cache_flash` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`)
used **key's head_size for the value side** (read stride 192 on width-128; 192-elem copy into 128-wide
region clobbering next head + cross-row overflow): patched with **intent-aligned per-side geometry**
(`v_head_size=value.size(2)`, `v_page_stride/v_head_stride`, per-side contiguity + branch lengths +
`max(head,d)` launch dim; guards: equal num-heads, equal block geometry; **symmetric callers
byte-identical** — verified exact 0.0 round-trip both orders + upstream `test_cache.py -k flash`
**732 passed**). Attention numerics: engine-faithful golden suite **6/6** in [0.18–0.37%] bf16 band
incl. real kv_split/3d+reduce, sinks+SWA `((127,0)`, MTP multi-token, 32K prefill; fault matrix 9/9 clean.

## Observed caveats (honest, all recorded raw)
1. **TTFT p95 outlier**: U's single 562.6 ms sample (gsm8k1, first 4.9k-tok request after 48-tok smoke)
   sets p95 on n=8; raw rows show the other three 4.9k-tok TTFTs at 228/39/39 ms. Tail claims need n≫8.
2. **Prefix-reuse asymmetry**: within the arm, U's later identical-25-shot-prefix prompts hit ~39 ms
   TTFT (prefix reused) while T's stayed ~245 ms flat. Same corpus/order/env — candidate follow-up:
   APC vs sliding-window/sink backend interaction. It *helps* U's p50; the synth-only rows (no shared
   prefix) still favor U (−7.7% p50-equivalent: 135.6–139.9 vs 144.4–148.5 ms).
3. **U-side known handicap present**: `Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by
   ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps`
   (T:0/U:1) — U wins *despite* this per-draft-step metadata rebuild cost.
4. Null-content completions (reasoning-only): T 4/1319 vs U 3/1319 (parity).
5. Severity note: deltas from n=8 bench + 2 gsm8k runs each; treat as strong signal, not final CI numbers.

- `ab.sh` — protocol (plan/compare drily safe; arm = boot→gates→kv→bench(cold)→gsm8k→dump→summary;

    @classmethod
    def customize_spec(cls, spec: "AttentionSpec") -> "AttentionSpec":
        """Per-token-head modes pack inline fp32 scales after each head's
        data, so the content is (data + one scale) per K/V side."""
        mode = spec.kv_quant_mode
        if spec.state_content_bytes is not None or not mode.is_per_token_head:
            return spec
        hs_k, hs_v = spec.head_size, spec.head_size_v
        if mode == KVQuantMode.INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD:
            hs_k, hs_v = hs_k // 2, hs_v // 2
        scale_bytes = get_dtype_size(torch.float32)
        content = (hs_k + hs_v) * get_dtype_size(spec.dtype) + 2 * scale_bytes
        return replace(spec, state_content_bytes=content)

So candidate is likely blocked; a check costs one grep/compile log (compilation pass logs "supports_rope" decisions... maybe logs at graph compile).

OK. I think I have enough for a grounded answer. But maybe I should also check aiter UA kernel upstream opportunities: e.g., `get_preferred_block_size` UA returns 64; we forced 16 for LMCache. Does block-size 16 hurt UA kernel perf? bs16→more blocks; the TPOT −84% was vs DiffKV with LMCache transfer broken. Actually in vllm_bench, UA+bs16 vs DiffKV-default (bs16 presumably? DiffKV default preferred block size might be 16). Was UA at its preferred 64 measured with LMCache? LMCache transfer launch error at 64 → must use 16. So UA forced off its preferred block size; potential optimization: LMCache support for 64-byte... that's LMCache-side (upstream-track).

Yes — dropping **P9 (`AITER_ONLINE_TUNE`)** leaves plenty. Based on the record plus a fresh check of our tree, here's what "more from UA" actually looks like, ranked by (measured impact × confidence ÷ effort):

## Where UA left us
Closed win (`aiter-unified-ab/REPORT.md`): UA = TPOT **−16%**, TTFT p50 **−29%**, warm-up TTFT −74%, accuracy/acceptance/KV parity; with LMCache + `--block-size 16` at 154k-in: **TPOT −84% (6.3×), output 2.95×**. But the report explicitly records **U's one handicap**, logged on every boot:

> `Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.`

## A) Directly UA-backend items (the "more UA" list)

**A1. Remove the handicap: enable fused multi-step draft decode for UA** ← best UA-specific candidate
- I verified locally: `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` defaults **False** (`v1/attention/backend.py:591`), and `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py` never sets it / has no `update_draft_decode_metadata` — hence the fallback at `speculator.py:111-122`. `triton_attn.py:270` sets it True with a **no-op** update — i.e. the opt-in shape is small; framework support (#46849) is already merged on our tree.
- Evidence: upstream **#52628** (ROCm opt-in, validated **with exactly `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` + MTP k=3**, GSM8K parity, **+2.13% c16 / +1.30% c128** on MI355X) is open/needs-rebase; #54369 shows the per-draft-step metadata rebuild is the tax that caps useful k at 4 — so this also unlocks deeper drafting (feeds P5b cascade).
- Cost: M (port #52628 or hand-implement on our UA builder), risk M (verification-batch correctness, #54039-class hang watch). Letter gates: gsm8k ±1.0pp, acceptance parity, TPOT.

**A2. Port `#49170` UA Triton warmup** — confirmed **absent** from our tree and wheel (`nextstep_2_local.md` A). This is behind our TTFT p95 outlier (562.6 ms — first real request after smoke) and the warmup row. Effort M (needs upstream diff + rebase), risk L, and it **gates any TTFT-tail claim** we make about UA.

**A3. Turn on the RoPE+KV-cache-write fusion for our UA config** — currently silently *off* for us
- Our boot config (`server_info`): `optimization_level: 2` but `fuse_rope_kvcache: false`, `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache: false`, `enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion: false`.
- Traced why (zero-run): the O2 predicate `enable_rope_kvcache_fusion` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:204-217`) requires `+rotary_embedding` custom op **and** (`use_inductor_graph_partition` **or** no kv-cache-update in `splitting_ops`) — ours has `use_inductor_graph_partition=false` **and** `splitting_ops` explicitly contains `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` → False (same logic warns at `config/compilation.py:1168-1177`). UA *does* expose the hooks (`fused_rope_kvcache_supported → rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled()`, `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py:355`).
- Win if valid: one HIP kernel instead of rope-then-cache-write on **every decode + MTP draft step** (≤256 tokens, `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num`), fewer launches, no intermediate roundtrip — benefits TPOT directly.
- **Caveat that must be checked first:** our K/V head geometry is asymmetric (K 192 / V 128) — exactly the class of bug we root-caused in RC-W2 (`reshape_and_cache_flash` using K's head_size for the V side). The QK-norm variant hard-supports only head dims {64,128,256} (would skip 192). So: verify the plain `fuse_rope_kvcache` kernel's per-side geometry support, then one letter with the golden suite + gsm8k as gate.

**A4. Block-size 64 vs LMCache-forced 16** — UA prefers `get_preferred_block_size→64`; LMCache transfer breaks at 64 (`hipErrorInvalidConfiguration`), so we pin 16. We never measured UA@64-without-LMCache vs 16 → either a 1-run letter to quantify what bs16 costs us, or upstream-track LMCache accepting 64 (doc'd in the `vllm_bench` addendum).

**A5. UA kernel config/tuning on gfx950** — aiter has UA tuning only for gfx1151 (aiter#5601) and an open LDS config-selection bug (#4329); our shapes are untuned. This is attention-side (distinct from the rejected MoE online-tune — that knob doesn't even cover attention), so treat as **upstream-track/watch only** unless you want to own tuned rows.

## B) Backend-independent backlog that still dominates (unchanged by UA)
- **P2 — the headline** (`nextstep_3_verdict.md`): ext-hit ⇒ no local-APC backfill under HMA = **~28.6 GB cross-replica KV per request, 11/12 requests pay it**; read-only root-cause pass over `kv_cache_coordinator.py` + `_annotate_eagle_groups` first, then fix letter on our branch. Still the largest measured cost in the whole stack.
- **P1** `draft_sample_method: "probabilistic"` — one JSON key, upstream +2…7pp acceptance (5 PRs merged); precondition = confirm runner identity (MRV1/MRV2) from boot log.
- **P4** fp8-KV — merge-wait on **#58128** (≈×2 KV budget), then narrow-gate A/B. `gh pr watch 58128`.
- **P7** `--max-num-batched-tokens` 8192/32768 vs 16384 (prefill-dominant) · **P3** consistent-hash affinity routing · **P8** acceptance-vs-context curve (gates P5b multi-layer cascade) · **P6** async-scheduling risk pin (currently `true` in our config).

**Watch queue (one line):** `gh pr watch 58128,52628,49170,58141,58650,58798` — #58141 (+8% decode multi-token split-KV) and #58650 are DiffKV-family but the *concept* is what UA's verify-batch path would want; #58798 is MiMo-specific but CUDA-only as written.

## Suggested order
1. **P2 read + fix letter** (largest measured cost, zero-run to start, rides our existing branch authority) — the standing headline.
2. **A1 fused multi-step draft** (removes UA's only handicap; small code, one letter).
3. **A3 verify-then-letter** for rope+kv fusion (traced blocker is config-level; correctness gate because of our K192/V128 history).
4. **A2 warmup port** + **P1/P7 letters** (cheap, parallelizable).
5. Queue P4 behind #58128, A4 as a 1-run quantification.

{"body":"## Purpose

Adds a dedicated warmup pass that precompiles the AITER unified-attention Triton
kernels (`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` backend) during vLLM startup, so their JIT
compilation cost is paid once at warmup time instead of on the critical path of
the first user requests.
This mirrors the existing warmup modules (e.g. `sparse_mla_triton_warmup`,
`flashinfer_sparse_mla_decode_autotune_warmup`) and hooks into the shared
`kernel_warmup(worker)` entry point.

### What changed

- **New module `vllm/model_executor/warmup/rocm_aiter_unified_attn_warmup.py`:**
  - Discovers every attention layer using the `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` backend
    and deduplicates them by a compile-relevant `_AttnSignature`
    (heads, KV heads, head size, block size, num blocks, sliding window, KV-cache
    dtype, sinks, query dtype), so each unique configuration is warmed exactly
    once.
  - Derives an input-space sweep from the live vLLM config (`max_model_len`,
    `max_num_seqs`, `max_num_batched_tokens`, and speculative-decoding token
    count).
  - Builds a set of representative launch specs that exercise the different
    kernel code paths:
    - **Prefill** launches (2D kernel) across power-of-two query lengths.
    - **Decode** launches (small-q) that hit both the 2D kernel (small context)
      and the 3D + reduce path (large context) across power-of-two context
      lengths and batch sizes.
    - **Non-decode small-q** launches (e.g. speculative decoding, `ALL_DECODE=False`).
    - A **mixed varlen** prefill+decode batch that hits both kernels together and
      reaches AITER's large-prefill (`>= 256`) config where the budget allows.
  - Launches `unified_attention` against the real KV cache with zero-filled
    query/output tensors and valid block tables (warmup only reads the cache),
    handling both uniform and varlen (`cu_seqlens_q`) batches, and quantized
    (fp8) KV caches.
  - Runs under `torch.inference_mode()`, synchronizes the accelerator afterward,
    and is fully best-effort: any failure is logged as a warning and skipped
    rather than aborting startup.
- **`vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`:**
  - Imports and calls `rocm_aiter_unified_attn_warmup_if_needed(worker)` as part
    of the standard kernel warmup sequence.

### Data quantifying the cost of the per-draft-step metadata rebuild

I re-ran the MTP depth sweep with a proper methodology and the numbers now isolate the overhead cleanly.

**Method** (previous numbers in this issue used a home-grown burst harness with ±30 % run-to-run spread — disregard those): `vllm bench serve` against a realistic-prose custom dataset, warmup round then measurement, ±5.5 % spread. Random-token datasets are useless here: on identical hardware they give 11.96 % draft acceptance versus 51.86 % on real text, because the draft head cannot predict random tokens.

8x MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, 48 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens:

| `num_speculative_tokens` | acceptance length | output tok/s | mean TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.44 | 1 452 | 28.8 ms |
| **4** | 3.05 | **1 642** | 24.7 ms |
| 6 | 3.33 | 1 623 | 25.5 ms |
| 8 | 3.52 | 1 155 | 35.7 ms |

**Acceptance length rises monotonically with k — the draft head keeps producing useful tokens all the way to k=8 — but throughput peaks at k=4 and collapses by 30 % at k=8.** The draft quality is not the limit; the per-step cost is.

That is the signature of the fallback this issue is about: with `use_fused_multi_step_decode == False`, `_multi_step_decode` calls `compute_slot_mappings` and rebuilds the attention metadata inside the loop, once per draft step, whereas `_fused_multi_step_decode` does it once before the loop. At k=8 that is seven extra rebuilds per decode step.

A rough upper bound on what fusing would buy: if the extra draft steps were free, k=8 (acceptance 3.52) over k=4 (3.05) is ~15 % more accepted tokens per verify. Today that shows up as a 30 % loss instead.

One more datapoint on where the cost sits: at this operating point the sparse-indexer plan is *not* rebuilt between draft steps, because `metadata_key` clamps `seq_lens` to `topk_tokens` (2048) — for contexts above 2048 the key is unchanged across draft steps and the planner (including its `torch.cuda.synchronize()`) is skipped. So the remaining per-step cost is the slot-mapping and metadata construction itself, not the aiter planner.

Happy to test a patch on this hardware if someone wants to attempt hoisting the metadata build for `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` / `DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER` / `KPOOL_TAIL`.


--- stefanskiasan 2026-08-30T15:33:19Z
### Enabled it — the three backends can use the fused path as-is

Following up on my own issue: the three backends only ever needed to opt in. `triton_attn` implements `update_draft_decode_metadata` as an empty method, because the framework already advances positions, `seq_lens` and slot mappings between draft steps — the metadata just references them. The same holds here:

```python
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py
#   class ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
#   class DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder, class KpoolTailMetadataBuilder

    supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = True

    def update_draft_decode_metadata(self, _metadata) -> None:
        pass
```

With that the startup warning disappears and `_fused_multi_step_decode` runs. **Correctness holds**: acceptance length is unchanged at 3.05 (it was 3.06 before). That is the sharp check — stale draft metadata would degrade the drafts immediately and acceptance would collapse, so an unchanged acceptance rate over a full benchmark is strong evidence the empty hook is valid here.

For the sparse indexer specifically there is a second reason it is safe at realistic context lengths: `metadata_key` in `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build` clamps `seq_lens` to `topk_tokens` (2048), so for any context above 2048 the key does not change across draft steps and the aiter planner is skipped anyway.

**Throughput** (8x MI350X gfx950, TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, `vllm bench serve`, realistic-prose dataset, three warmup passes, 96 concurrent, 256 output tokens):

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (per-step rebuild) | 2 962 | 27.2 ms | 3.06 |
| after (fused) | **3 043** | **26.4 ms** | 3.05 |

Only +2.7 %, well short of what the cost decomposition predicted. `compute_slot_mappings` still runs per step in the fused path; what is saved is `build_slot_mappings_by_layer` (a Python dict across all 45 layers) plus `_build_draft_attn_metadata`. The rest of the per-step cost sits elsewhere.

### The bigger finding: on this MoE, k=1 beats k=4

Same setup, sweeping depth with the fused path enabled, 96 concurrent:

| `num_speculative_tokens` | acceptance length | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | 1.83 | **3 155** |
| 2 | 2.43 | 2 794 |
| 4 | 3.05 | 3 043 |

Acceptance rises with k as expected, but throughput does not follow. Decomposing step time (TPOT × acceptance length) across concurrency gives a fixed per-step cost of **34.4 ms at k=4 versus 20.5 ms at k=1** — about **4.6 ms of pure overhead per draft step**, against a draft head that is a single layer out of 45 and should cost roughly 1 ms.

Part of this looks structural rather than framework overhead: on a dense model rejected draft tokens are nearly free, but on a 288-expert MoE the verify pass over 5 tokens instead of 1 means proportionally more expert invocations, and at k=4 two of every five verified tokens are discarded.

So for MoE models the right default may be much shallower speculation than for dense ones — worth documenting, and worth a second look at whether the remaining per-draft-step cost can be hoisted further. Happy to test patches on this hardware.

remainder, and it is not small.

## Measurement

py-spy on the worker busy loop, 40 s under load, 16 k-context dataset:

```
samples in worker_busy_loop: 7997
 38.78 %  seq_lens_cpu (vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:473)
 22.63 %  poll  (waiting for work from the scheduler)
  4.64 %  LMCache get_finished
  3.40 %  from_ipc_handle
```

Split by caller — it is essentially all draft path:

```
38.25 %  _fused_multi_step_decode -> _build_draft_attn_metadata
         -> build_attn_metadata -> rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.build -> seq_lens_cpu
 0.53 %  execute_model -> prepare_attn -> ... -> seq_lens_cpu
```

So on this backend the fallback costs far more through the metadata *key* than
through the metadata *build* it is meant to guard.

## Why `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` is the outlier

`seq_lens_cpu` is the deprecated `_seq_lens_cpu` field ("removed in v0.15.0").
`seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` landed in #40654 precisely to avoid this sync, and
the other backends took it: `flash_attn`, `mla/indexer`, `mla/sparse_swa`,
`mamba_attn`, `mamba2_attn`, `flex_attention`, `cross_attention`. Every other
speculator path reads the CPU bound too:

```
spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py:236   seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound[...].max().item()
spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py:161 seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound[...].max().item()
spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py:347           seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound[...].max().item()
```

"""Shared interfaces and tracing helpers for explicit JIT warmup keys."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import builtins
import inspect
import itertools
import operator
import textwrap
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator, Mapping
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
from functools import wraps
from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar, cast

__all__ = [
    "JitWarmupRegistry",
    "VllmJitKernel",
    "WarmupChoices",
    "WarmupIntRange",
    "get_ast_full_name",
    "get_function_source_node",
    "kernel_launcher",
    "zip_inputs",
]


CompileKeyT = TypeVar("CompileKeyT")


def kernel_launcher(call_fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Delegate a declarative launch specification to its backend owner."""
    signature = inspect.signature(call_fn)

    @wraps(call_fn)
    def wrapper(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        launch_spec = call_fn(self, *args, **kwargs)
        if not self.bind_launch_inputs:
            return self.launch(launch_spec, {})

        bound = signature.bind(self, *args, **kwargs)
        bound.apply_defaults()
        inputs = {
            name: value for name, value in bound.arguments.items() if name != "self"
        }
        return self.launch(launch_spec, inputs)

    return wrapper

I pulled the actual PR/issue threads and cross-checked them against our own logs. That changed my ranking in both directions — and yes, the #49170 comment thread is damning in a way our notes missed. Here's my own assessment, item by item.

## What the primary evidence changed

**1. #49170 (UA warmup): reviewer objection is real, but the premise also turned out true for us — verdict: don't port the PR, fix it ourselves differently**
- The only substantive review comment (AndreasKaratzas, 07-21): *"I am not sure about this. AITER is built with PRECOMPILED_KERNELS=1. What kernels are still being compiled?"* — **never answered**, PR went `dirty`/needs-rebase and stalled 2 months. Its entire "Test Result" is one log line where the `jit_monitor` warning disappears — **zero latency measurements**, tested on Mistral-7B/MI350X.
- But I checked *our* UA arm log: the premise does hold first-party — `WARNING ... Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: kernel_unified_attention_2d` (14:22:06), then `kernel_unified_attention_3d` + `reduce_segments` (14:22:08). These are *Triton* JITs (not hipcc, so PRECOMPILED_KERNELS doesn't cover them — the reviewer's objection is answerable, just never was). The 562 ms p95 outlier sits exactly in that window.
- **Crucially, our warnings also list three kernels #49170 does NOT cover**: `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`, `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` (spec-decode). So porting the PR wouldn't even clear our warnings — it targets 3 of our 5.
- **My call: reject the port.** Unreviewed, unquantified, conflict-dirty, sweep would scale with `max_model_len=100000`. Instead: (a) zero-run — check whether Triton's cache persists across our boots (is this every-boot or cache-cold only?); (b) fix our *bench protocol* with a proper warm round (long-prefill + one full 600-tok generation before measuring) — fixes our numbers today, zero code; (c) if production first-token matters, register **our exact 5-kernel list** in the existing declarative `jit_warmup` registry (we have better evidence than the PR does).

**2. A1 fused multi-step draft — upstream fact changed under us; also its value was oversold**
- #52628 is `CONFLICTING`; AMD's own follow-up (**draft #58352**, 09-23) rebases it *and* fixes the hot `build()` path: 48→28 µs/call, 6 launches/3 allocs→2/0. → track/port **#58352's pattern**, not the stale #52628.
- The issue author's own follow-up on **8×MI350X gfx950** after enabling the fused path: **+2.7% only** ("well short of what the cost decomposition predicted"), correct gate = acceptance unchanged (3.06→3.05). The +8–13% numbers I quoted earlier were stale PR-era claims. So expectation for us ≈ **+1–3% decode**, not more.
- Bigger fish in their py-spy: **38.8% of worker busy loop in `seq_lens_cpu`** — a deprecated G2G-sync field — and UA's builder is *not* in the `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` adopter list I grepped. Whether our UA `build()` hits that sync per draft step is a **local grep I haven't finished** — if it does, that's a larger, better-targeted fix than the fuse flag, and it's on our 3.6 ms-TPOT hot path.
- **My call: conditional.** Pre-req = the `seq_lens_cpu` grep on the UA/Rocm builder. If clean or cheap, the opt-in itself may be literally `supports_draft_decode_decode_metadata_update = True` + empty hook (their evidence shows the framework advances positions/slot mappings; acceptance-parity is the sharp gate).

**3. NEW — the cheapest big lever nobody put on our list: sweep k ∈ {1,2,3}**
- #54369's gfx950 measurement: on a **288-expert MoE, k=1 beat k=4** (3155 vs 3043 tok/s) despite monotonic acceptance — ~4.6 ms fixed overhead per draft step plus verify-pass waste (2/5 tokens discarded, each activating experts). Our model *is* MoE (256 experts).
- We inherited **k=3 from the recipe**; our docs rejected **k>3** — but **k<3 was never tested on our stack**. We know k=0→k=3 = 6.2→4.1 ms TPOT, nothing between. If k=2 sits at ~2.5 acceptance with one less draft step, it may beat k=3 end-to-end — and it's one flag × 3 runs on the existing harness.
- This also directly undercuts **P5b's economics** (deeper cascade = more MoE verify waste) → P8 + this k-sweep must gate any P5b engineering.

**4. A3 rope+KV-cache fusion — I'm demoting it.** I traced why O2 leaves it off (predicate fails on `use_inductor_graph_partition=false` + `unified_kv_cache_update` in `splitting_ops`), but judging further: the fusion only covers ≤256-token steps (decode; graphs already amortize launches there), enabling it *flips piecewise-cudagraph structure* (confounded A/B), and the per-side-head geometry risk is exactly the K192/V128 class we already root-caused once (RC-W2). Ceiling low, risk non-zero → shelve unless a trace shows those boundaries are hot.

**5. A4 block-size 64 — effectively moot.** LMCache is mandatory (operator ruling) and 64 breaks its transfer, so 16 isn't a tunable anymore, it's a constraint. Drop.

**6. A5 aiter tuned-configs — watch-only, respecting your ruling.** Our UA boot shows **4,286 `not found tuned config`** lines, but that's GEMM/MoE shape debt (aiter-side, model-specific rows; no attention online-tune hook exists). Not our lane after dropping P9.

**7. P2 backfill — keep #1, but I'm re-scoping the prize honestly.** My earlier "−80…90%" repeated *bytes* as if it were *time*. From our own logs: HMA-on TTFT at 240k = 10,795 vs 10,091 ms off → the observed wall-clock cost is ≈ **+7% TTFT**, plus host-memory/replica-scaling pressure. Also the r1=249,952 / r2=0 asymmetry is unexplained, and the owed retrieval-seconds@240k read still hasn't been done. **Measure first (zero-run on existing logs), then decide** whether the fix belongs in the vLLM coordinator or the LMCache connector (#1096 family) — diagnosis may land on the cheap side.

**8. P1 probabilistic — stays high (my own strongest conviction).** Official sampling is temp=1.0 → greedy verify systematically under-accepts exactly where we're weakest (per-pos .65/.33); one JSON key; evidence is 5 merged+hardened PRs. Expectation: +1–3pp acceptance.

**9. P7 — keep** (32768 halves a 150k prompt from 15→8 chunks). And a correction: the official `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` we run as `NONE` is a **no-op at TP1** (no all-reduce) → correctly ignore until TP>1.

**10. P4 fp8-KV — geopolitically better than the docs say, still gated.** My own synthesis: for *our* stack it compounds — halves GPU KV budget **and** LMCache host/wire bytes, i.e. it attacks the same 28.6 GB/request problem P2 attacks. Against: upstream's +15% TTFT@128K collides directly with our 154k-in profile, and ROCm validation count = 0 (we *would be* the validation). Verdict: unchanged gate (#58128), but treat it as a flagship first-party contribution, not a consumer flag.

**11. P3 affinity — downgrade.** Our own 6k measurement was ≈0 (noise); it only pays with multiple replicas + hot shared prefixes. Sequence it *after* P2's measurement, not alongside.

**12. Watch-queue trim post-UA:** #58141 / #58650 / #58798 are all **DiffKV-family — we left that backend**, so their relevance to us collapsed; drop to background. Keep #58128, #58352 + #52628 + #54369 (draft-metadata family), #49170 (context only).

## My revised sequence

- **Phase 0 (zero-run):** (i) does the UA/Rocm builder read `seq_lens_cpu`? (ii) Triton-cache persistence across boots → sizes the JIT issue; (iii) retrieval-seconds@240k from existing bench_lctx logs → P2's ceiling; (iv) decide warm-protocol vs jit_warmup registration from our 5-kernel list.
- **Phase 1 (first GPU letters, shared harness):** **k-sweep 1/2/3** (new, cheapest, potentially largest) and **P1 probabilistic** — before any code. Pre-check GPU ownership; the last chain hit the occupancy guard and the `on`-arm left leaked semaphores.
- **Phase 2:** P2 diagnosis → fix letter wherever the defect site actually is; A1 opt-in only if the `seq_lens_cpu` pre-req comes back cheap and #58352 hasn't landed.
- **Phase 3:** P7, P3-after-P2; P4 the day #58128 merges; P8 + k-sweep results gate any P5b decision.

The meta-correction: last time I ranked *documents*; the threads show two of my "M-effort/low-risk" items were stalls (#49170 unanswered objection, #52628 superseded by #58352), one number was stale (+8–13% → +2.7%), and the biggest cheap opportunity (k<3) was invisible because a rejection got over-generalized.

# FP8 KV cache — re-exploration, 2026-09-26

## 1. The old blocker stack dissolved — mostly

When we closed this, the story was: *no-op → two-stage root cause → blocked on upstream PR #58128*. Re-checked:

- **UA already supports fp8 KV end-to-end.** First-party: `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py:57-63` declares `supported_kv_cache_dtypes` **including `fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`**, with real quantized-KV code paths (`key_cache.view(self.fp8_dtype)` at :265-267, `k_descale/v_descale` plumbing at :291/:321). The aiter kernel behind it is fp8-native (`unified_attention.py:204 K_WIDTH = 16 if kv_cache_dtype == e4m3`, `IS_KV_FP8`, `k_scale_ptr=params.k_descale` at :844). The cache-write kernel has FP8 instantiations (`cache_kernels.cu:1127-1209`) — and it's the *same templated kernel we repaired in RC-W2* (per-side K192/V128 geometry), so the fp8 store path inherited our fix.
- **⇒ #58128's attention half is now irrelevant to us.** Its diff (fetched) = 5 files: `triton_attn_diffkv.py` + `triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py` + diffkv test (**the fp8-kernel half — we don't need it, we left DiffKV**), plus `mimo_v2.py +7` / `mimo_v2_mtp.py +6` — **the model-side `cache_config` forwarding, which is the only part that ever blocked us**.
- **#58128 status today:** open, `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: blocked` (CI/review), updated 09-24; maintainer (lucamotz) active — folding the closed #58176, explicitly planning quality comparisons ("since the cluster can now do some extended testing"). A GB10 commenter independently hit *our exact bug* ("MiMoV2DecoderLayer builds MiMoV2Attention without cache_config, still true on current main") with stock numbers: 840,536 tok bf16 @ 66.3K tok/GiB.

**Verified on our branch — all three call sites still omit it** (`mimo_v2.py:396` SWA, `:416` global, `mimo_v2_mtp.py:88`; the class accepts `cache_config` at :233 and forwards to `Attention` at :350, but nobody passes it; `Attention.__init__` then defaults `kv_cache_dtype="auto"` — attention.py:278-281). MTP's ctor doesn't even have the parameter → port threads it.

**One subtle trap worth knowing before we touch it:** #58128 passes `copy.copy(cache_config)` with **`sliding_window=None` for global layers**, because `cache_config.sliding_window=128` would otherwise leak into global layers via Attention's model-level fallback — a naive 3-line port would silently turn the 9 global layers into SWA. The port is small but not *trivial*.

## 2. Why it's worth more on our stack than upstream's framing

| axis | upstream (GB10/DiffKV) | ours (2×gfx950, UA, LMCache+HMA+MTP) |
|---|---|---|
| GPU KV budget | ×2.0003 measured | 870,985 tok / 8.71× → **expect ~1.65–1.75M (~17×)**; skip-SWA variant retains ~90%+ of the win at our contexts (9 global layers carry nearly all bytes; SWA groups are window-bounded at 128) |
| LMCache host/wire | — | `metadata.kv_dtype` drives the store (`gpu_connector/__init__.py:91`) and fp8 maps exist (`lmcache/utils.py:366`) → 125,440 → **~62,720 B/tok**; the 28.6 GB cross-replica retrieve → **~14.3 GB/req** — *compounds directly with P2* |
| accuracy | GSM8K 0.933→0.943, needles 8/8+4/4 | unvalidated — gates below (our band .9727 is tight enough to catch failure instantly) |

So for us fp8-KV is not just capacity: it's a **second independent attack on our #1 measured recurring cost** (cross-replica bytes), and capacity that matters for our 100k-max-model-len profile.

## 3. Honest costs/risks

- **TTFT prefill regression: +4–7% @16–32k, +15% @128k upstream** — collides head-on with our 154k-in workload. Decode flat. Nobody has measured fp8-KV *prefill on UA/gfx950* → this is the number our letter must produce; if it's real at 128k+, the decision becomes capacity×2 vs TTFT, possibly per-workload.
- **Zero public ROCm validation exists** — we'd be first (also makes our data a *contribution* to a PR that's explicitly asking for quality data → helps it merge).
- **Mixed-dtype store (skip variant):** fp8 global + bf16 SWA in one LMCache store object — the connector takes **one** `kv_dtype`. This is the biggest unknown for combining skip-SWA *with* LMCache; `skip_page_size_padded` machinery exists in-tree for page alignment, but the store path is unverified → order the cells GPU-only first, LMCache-on second.
- Cross-dtype store reuse (the kvfp8-ab cell-C hole): pin store hygiene per cell; read `lmcache describe` dtype/B-tok — never trust absence-of-errors (LMCache #4247 lesson).
- fp8 round-trip through our *patched* write kernel at K192/V128: upstream's 732 flash tests ran, but I can't confirm they cover our exact geometry+fp8 → one cheap GPU unit probe first.
- New fp8 kernel variants → first-request JIT spike returns → warm round in the bench protocol (yesterday's jit_monitor finding).
- MTP draft layer uses the **SWA config** → under `skip sliding_window` the draft stays bf16 (probably good for acceptance; it also means skip-variant semantics we should state explicitly in the letter).

## 4. Adjacent finds from this pass (the "related improvement" part)

1. **LMCache `remote_serde` (default `naive`)** with **TurboQuant presets** (`turboquant_k8v4`, `k3v4_nc`, `4bit_nc`, `k3v4` — compress before store/transfer) — a *wire/host compression* lever on our 28.6 GB that is independent of fp8 **and** of P2's backfill fix. Unknown: whether our cross-replica (MP/localhost) path routes through the remote backend that consumes it — one config probe answers it.
2. **vLLM has a whole `turboquant_attn` backend** (registry `TURBOQUANT`, `kv_cache_dtype turboquant_*` modes, flydsl decode kernels, the AMD/UltraQuant lineage): k8v4 ≈ 0.38× bytes/token native — far deeper than fp8's 0.5×. **My judgment: watch-only.** It's its own attention backend, i.e. we'd trade away UA (our proven −16% TPOT), K192/V128 support unverified, and it competes with rather than stacks on what works. Recording it so the regime is mapped, not adopting it.

## 5. My proposed sequence

**Phase 0 (zero/cheap, hours):** new workdir per AGENTS.md (`fp8-kv-ua-gfx950/`) capturing this; port **#58128's model-side half only** (with the `sliding_window=None` copy) as a reviewable letter branch on top of `custom/ua-mimo-gfx942`, upstream-linked; one-GPU probe: fp8 write/read round-trip at K192/V128 through our patched kernel.

**Phase 1 (letters on the existing harness, LMCache OFF first):**
- **A**: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (all layers) · **B**: + `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers sliding_window` (official AMD recipe; draft stays bf16) — vs today's recorded baseline.
- Gates: boot dtype/backend lines · budget ≈×1.9–2.0 vs 870,985 · gsm8k within ±1.0pp of .9727 · MTP acceptance parity ~0.666 · 128k needle · **TTFT@~128–154k explicitly** (the upstream regression) · decode TPOT flat-equivalent.

**Phase 2 (LMCache/HMA on):** `lmcache describe` B/tok 125,440→~62,720 · ext-hit rate · 250k `bench_lctx`-style run → **retrieval-seconds@240k, the measurement P2 has owed all along** (fp8 halves bytes; backfill fix removes the request — the two together give the full picture).

**Phase 3:** post our gfx950 tables on #58128 (maintainer is literally asking for this), then decide port-vs-wait.

Net: the regime moved from "blocked-on-merge" to "**portable today, validation-gated, and stacked with P2 + possibly LMCache serde**" — with prefill-TTFT as the one number only we can produce.

arguments.content:
# fp8-kv-ua-gfx950 — does fp8 KV cache work on UA + gfx950 *now*?

**Question (operator 2026-09-26):** not "port the upstream PR" — the empirical question is whether
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` actually works end-to-end with `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` on 2×gfx950
(MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL). No LMCache in this first cell. TurboQuant explicitly out of scope (operator).
Branch: build ontop of **`custom/ua-mimo-gfx942`** @ 3430f806f0 (+ local uncommitted model-side edit).

## Why this was ever "blocked" — and why it isn't anymore

Old record (`mimo-explore/kvfp8-ab`, `kv-dtype-rootcause`): `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` was a silent
no-op, two-stage root cause:
1. **model side:** `mimo_v2.py` / `mimo_v2_mtp.py` built `MiMoV2Attention` without `cache_config`
   → `Attention(cache_config=None)` → per-layer `kv_cache_dtype="auto"` (attention.py:278-281) →
   store silently stays bf16. Fix lives in **open PR #58128** (model half = +13 LOC across the two
   files; the DiffKV half +31 LOC is **irrelevant to us** — we left DiffKV for UA).
2. **attention side:** TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV had no fp8 kernel → **does not apply to UA**:
   - `rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py:57-63` declares `supported_kv_cache_dtypes` incl. `fp8`,
     `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`; quantized paths live (`key_cache.view(self.fp8_dtype)` :265-267,
     `k_descale/v_descale` plumbing :291/:321).
   - aiter kernel `unified_attention.py`: `IS_KV_FP8`, `K_WIDTH = 16 if kv_cache_dtype == e4m3`
     (:204), `k_scale_ptr=params.k_descale` (:844).
   - cache-write kernel `cache_kernels.cu` has FP8 instantiations (:1127-1209) in the **same
     templated kernel we repaired in RC-W2** (per-side K192/V128 geometry) — fp8 store inherits it.

⇒ Only prerequisite = the model-side forward. Decision: apply it locally on the branch (operator:
goal is "does it work", not a portable port; keep it attributable).

## Change under test (uncommitted, on custom/ua-mimo-gfx942)

- `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` +9: `import copy`; `cache_config = copy.copy(...)`;
  `cache_config.sliding_window = None` (mirrors #58128 — **without this, Attention's model-level
  fallback would give the 9 global layers SWA window 128**); `cache_config=cache_config` at both
  `MiMoV2Attention(...)` call sites (SWA + global).
- `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_mtp.py` +7/-1: thread `CacheConfig` through
  `MiMoV2MTPLayer` → `_MiMoV2MTPLayers` → `MiMoV2MultiTokenPredictor` (from
  `vllm_config.cache_config`). MTP keeps its SWA window legitimately (no copy — as upstream).
- Verification: AST OK, module import OK, signatures carry `cache_config`.
- Diff vs branch HEAD: `git diff --stat` → 2 files, +16/−1. **Not committed** (revert = `git checkout -- <files>`).

## Protocol (mirrors `aiter-unified-ab/ab.sh` arm u = the proven UA reference)

- Single cell, GPU 0, port 58411, `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`,
  `--speculative-config {mtp,3}`, `--max-model-len 100000`, TP1, graphs on,
  **LMCache OFF** (no `--kv-transfer-config`), HMA on (env lever unset, same as reference),
  single delta vs arm-u = **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`** (+ the model-side enabler).
- `./run.sh boot | gates | bench | smoke | acc | summary | stop | all`
  - bench: same `bench.py` cold pass n=8 (u-arm baseline: p50 TTFT **137.1 ms**, TPOT **3.592 ms**)
  - acc: lm-eval gsm8k 25-shot full 1319 (u-arm baseline flex **0.9727 ±0.0045**)

## Gates (pass = "fp8 works on UA+gfx950")

| # | gate | expectation | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `backend_used` | `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` | u-arm |
| G2 | startup config | `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` (engine-level honest now) | was `auto` |
| G3 | budget line | `GPU KV cache size:` ≈ **×2** → ~1.6–1.75M tokens (16–17.5×) vs cu | **870,985 / 8.71×** — if ≈871k ⇒ still no-op somewhere |
| G4 | boot tracebacks / memory faults | 0 / 0 (fp8 path at graph capture = RC-K1 class watch) | 0/0 |
| G5 | smoke outputs | coherent (RC-W2 garbage-text class with scales now live) | — |
| G6 | gsm8k full flex | ≥ **0.9627** (u-arm 0.9727 ±0.01 gate) | 0.9727 |

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

model="XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL"
BACKEND=ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
PORT=58411
GPU=0; GPU_UTIL=0.9; MAX_LEN=100000; LMEVAL_MAXLEN=32000
KV_DTYPE="${KV_DTYPE:-fp8}"
V="logs"; R="results"
[ -f bench.py ] || cp -n ../mimo-explore/lmcache-mimo-v26/bench.py bench.py

alive()  { [[ -f "$1" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "$1" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null; }
stop_pidfile() {
    local pf="$1" p
    alive "$pf" || { rm -f "$pf"; return 1; }
    p=$(cat "$pf")
    kill -TERM -- "-$p" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
    local i; for i in $(seq 1 30); do kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
    kill -KILL -- "-$p" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$p"* 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f "$pf"; return 0
}
gpu_guard() {
    local v
    v=$(rocm-smi 2>/dev/null | awk -v g="$GPU" '$1==g{v=$(NF-1); gsub(/%/,"",v); print v; exit}')
    [[ -z "$v" ]] && { echo "  warn: cannot read VRAM% for GPU $GPU (continuing)"; return 0; }
    if (( v > 5 )) && [[ -z "${FORCE_GPU:-}" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: GPU $GPU shows VRAM ${v}% — occupancy not owned by us (FORCE_GPU=1 to override)." >&2; return 1
    fi

}
gate_put() { mkdir -p "$R"; local line="$1 $2"; touch "$R/gates.txt"
    grep -qxF "$line" "$R/gates.txt" || echo "$line" >> "$R/gates.txt"; }
wait_http() {
    local i
    for i in $(seq 1 900); do
        curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
        alive "$V/replica.pid" || { echo "serve :$PORT died:"; tail -60 "$V/replica.log"; return 1; }
        sleep 2
    done

}
build_args() {

               --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len "$MAX_LEN"
               --gpu-memory-utilization "$GPU_UTIL"
               --attention-backend "$BACKEND"
               --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

}
boot() {

    gpu_guard
    build_args
    if (exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/"$PORT") 2>/dev/null; then
        exec 3<&- 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "ERROR: port $PORT busy on host network"; exit 1
    fi
    unset VLLM_ALLOW_CHUNKED_LOCAL_ATTN_WITH_HYBRID_KV_CACHE || true
    echo "  starting $model :$PORT GPU $GPU backend=$BACKEND kv_dtype=$KV_DTYPE len=$MAX_LEN (mtp=3, lmcache=off)"

gates() {
    local log="$V/replica.log"

    [[ -z "$be" ]] && be=MISSING
    gate_put "" "backend_used=$be(expected=$BACKEND)"
    local dt; dt=$(grep -oE 'kv_cache_dtype=[a-z0-9_]+' "$log" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
    [[ -z "$dt" ]] && dt=MISSING
    gate_put "" "kv_cache_dtype=$dt(expected=$KV_DTYPE)"
    local budget; budget=$(grep -oE 'GPU KV cache size: [0-9,]+ tokens' "$log" | tail -1 | grep -oE '[0-9,]+' | tr -d ',')
    [[ -z "$budget" ]] && budget=0
    local tb; tb=$(grep -c 'Traceback (most recent call last)' "$log" || true)
    local mtp; mtp=$(grep -c 'speculator\|Speculative decoding' "$log" || true)
    gate_put "" "kv_budget_tokens=$budget(bf16_ref=870985, fp8_expect=1600000-1750000)"
    gate_put "" "boot_tracebacks=$tb(expected=0)"
    gate_put "" "mtp_log=$([[ $mtp -gt 0 ]] && echo seen || echo MISSING)"

b = int(sys.argv[1] or 0)

ratio = b / 870985

PY
}

smoke() {

        echo '--- smoke ---';      cat "$R/smoke.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo none
